resolved_or_reduced: January 2026 remains the newest public premises-level BDUK UPRN release observed and is published as 318 LAD CSV files
The BDUK release contains 28 documented columns and preserves UPRN both as numeric uprn and string-prefixed struprn
The BDUK premises base is epoch-pinned AddressBase Premium filtered for postal and non-demolished premises
A missing UPRN is not proof of no property or no connectivity because demolished derelict and post-epoch new-build cases can be absent
Approximately 4900 GIS contract premises are absent from the release because OS now categorises them as demolished
BDUK contracts and intervention scopes can change rapidly and recent changes may not be represented in a release
Approximately 3.7 percent of intervention premises are in more than one intervention
Voucher inclusion does not guarantee delivery and Superfast or Gigahub premises can be descoped
If a premises is in more than two GIS contracts the published date is taken from the lead contract usually the initial scope
Supplier names are not standardised and related legal or operational entities can appear under different names
BDUK geography assignment first uses UPRN to NSUL then postcode to NSPL or UPRN to ONSUD as fallbacks
Postcode fallback provenance must therefore be retained and cannot be treated as an exact UPRN-to-geography proof
BDUK plans updated releases alongside the latest OMR closure approximately every four months
OS NGD Address Theme is available only through OS Select+Build and not through OS NGD Features or Tiles APIs
OS NGD Address Theme has six feature types and uses UPRN as the primary cross-theme identifier
OS NGD Related Entity supplies crossreferencefeature crossreferenceid relationshiptype source and effective date fields
Related Entity schema version 3.0 launched 30 September 2025 while versions 1.0 and 2.0 remain maintenance schemas
Related Entity components contain no geometry and must be joined to their lifecycle feature type by exact UPRN
Related Entity temporal snapshots requested before a schema launch date may contain inconsistencies
Annual Full Supply orders represent 1 January and can return empty packages for feature types or schema versions released later in the year
Ofcom Planned Network Deployments 2026 is a forward-looking operator-plan product and not a current-coverage substitute
Ofcom defines high-confidence deployment plans as at least Low Level Design Complete with funding committed
Ofcom PND includes privately and publicly supported operator plans but excludes separate public-authority aspirations
Ofcom PND percentages use the Spring 2026 residential premises base of 30.5 million while all-premises results are separate
Planned network overlap and overbuild are expected and do not imply unique supplier or unique network delivery
HMLR INSPIRE July 2026 remains the current open polygon snapshot until the next first-Sunday publication
